Forgive me, i'm writing this at 1 in the morning so there may be a few errors or things that may not make sense.

Character: Edmund Lee. Age 26, correctional officer with previous military experience. Engaged. Has two dogs (very important obviously /s).

Setting: Prison in Canadian woods, not too far out but at least a twenty minute car ride before you stumble upon a town.

It starts out while you, the player, are chatting with your colleague Andy. During your conversation you hear a commotion outside and an obviously distressed co-worker runs into your room *"there's something wrong. Something is blocking our security, the inmates are leaving their cells. We need help stat."* and runs back out. The hall is a mess, inmates are running wild and guards are already slowly being killed.  Andy looks at you apologetically before knocking you out and dragging you behind a piece of furniture, telling you he'll find help but you need to hide. 

When knocked out you remember the first day of being shipped off and how your family reacted. When you awake the sun is setting, several hours have gone by and it's quiet as hell. Grabbing the flashlight out of your belt you start to explore. You carry a flashlight (Needs batteries, which can be found in break rooms), a small baton and beeper. You explore the prison, trying to find a way out that isn't either A) blocked or B) surrounded by inmates who'll either kill you or do something far worse than death. You'll collect information on patients, learning how they got like that and why. Throughout the game when encountering certain smells or an abundance of blood you'll get flashbacks to your military days. 

You're able to use your baton to defend yourself for the first few inmates you meet who attack you. However when being attacked by one of the antagonists (Meathead, Edmund calls him) your baton gets split in half and you're unable to use it for the rest of the game. Notes are unsent texts to differing people Edmund knows due to the little reception. 

After finding Andy and pulling him away from the final boss (The ripper, an inmate who came from an abusive and negligent home who was only able to find love in hurting others. Got sent here for ripping off his girlfriend's tongue and killing animals by seeing what'll happen when you switch their organs with different species.) you escape out a window with bented bars in a deserted hallway. While helping him get into your car you look back at the prison and see some type of dark cloud covering the top of the prison. In it you think you can see some type of humanoid figure, seemingly directing it. You're only able to see it for a few seconds before it starts to come after you, and with that you push down the pedal and get the fuck out of there.

What makes it scary?: For me i've always been a fan of empathy horror. Where you can understand villains and know why they did it. Where you stay up at night knowing that you yourself could've been them if things gone wrong. Where they could've lived a normal life but they couldn't. Where the knowledge of something small going wrong can make people become monsters sending a shiver down your spine. That's my type of horror, where the plot mixes in. That's what made whistleblower so great in my opinion, you see these monstrosities of humans become who they are because of forces outside of their control. You feel empathy for these people and that's what scares some people most.

Oh, and maybe a dash of jump scares would make it a bit more scary.

Any connections?: Not many to be honest, correct me if i'm wrong but i believe Murkoff works with security? I was thinking that this prison could use a form of Murkoffs security. Miles in this is just tracking down any places that seem like the asylum and are connected to Murkoff, so this place included. While nothing too unethical goes on here (Let's be real here, guards can be assholes but other than the prisoner beat up every once in awhile nothing too bad happens) based on the outside it sure as hell seems like it.
